songs.name: And We Bid You Good Night

ai_show_review.summary: High‑energy early‑68 set with blazing Lovelight and Alligator jams
ai_show_review.blurb: The show opens with a scorching Turn On Your Lovelight that segues into the classic Cryptical Envelopment pair before launching into an incendiary The Other One. Pigpen’s raw vocals dominate Alligator and Caution jams, while the dual drummers drive the improvisations. The Miller soundboard capture is crisp enough to showcase every fiery moment.
ai_show_review.review: Los Angeles, December 21 1968 – at the Shrine Exposition Hall the Dead delivered a blistering one‑set performance that still feels like a barn‑burner. After kicking off with Turn On Your Lovelight, the band wove through Cryptical Envelopment into a soaring The Other One before diving into an Alligator‑heavy middle section where Pigpen’s guttural vocals and harmonica cut through the wall of sound. The Alligator > Caution (Do Not Stop On Tracks) jam, bolstered by relentless drumming from Mickey and Bill, erupts into Feedback and closes with a heartfelt And We Bid You Good Night. Both available recordings are soundboard sources; the Charlie Miller tape stands out for its surprisingly good clarity despite some vintage hiss, making it the definitive way to hear this high‑octane early‑68 set.

best_recording.reason: Charlie Miller soundboard offers good clarity and full set coverage, capturing the band's fire with minimal tape hiss.

key_highlights: Turn On Your Lovelight launches the set with Pigpen’s powerhouse vocals.
Alligator > Caution sequence delivers ferocious improvisation and tight drumming.
The Other One showcases the band's early exploratory jams.
Miller soundboard captures crisp instrument separation despite tape hiss.
